events.summary: Heavy rain flooded about 300 houses across Gurudatta Layout, areas near Bheemanakatte lake in Hosakerehalli and BEML Layout, with gushing water sweeping away vehicles.
Rainwater entered at least 100 homes in BEML Layout after heavy overnight rain, with residents blaming slow stormwater drain construction; RR Nagar logged 177.6 mm (Weather Union).
A stormwater drain breach sent sewage water into over 300 houses in Gurudatta Layout and Dattatreya Nagar, with officials expecting the toll to cross 500 including BEML and Pramod Layouts.
Heavy rain sparked fears of a breach in Hosakerehalli Lake, causing panic among thousands of residents in south Bengaluru.
Hosakerehalli lake overflowed in an evening downpour, sending sewage-mixed water into streets with knee-deep water for about two hours.
The retention wall of a stormwater drain at Pramod Layout breached, and residents pumped five to seven feet of water out of basements.
Pramod Layout was among the RR Nagar areas worst hit when overflowing stormwater drains flooded homes.
Overflowing stormwater drains from Hosakerehalli flooded Pramod Layout, worsened by a collapsing BBMP-built sidewall.
The basement of an apartment in RR Nagar's Ideal Homes layout was flooded up to one foot after overnight rain.
Heavy rain flooded several private layouts including Ideal Homes Layout, Nagarbhavi and Nayandahalli.
Ten cars were damaged after water entered an apartment complex at Kenchenahalli, as RR Nagar and Jnanabharathi got about 106 mm in one night.
Rajarajeshwari Nagar was among the worst-affected areas of an evening downpour, with water levels rising up to four feet.
A stormwater drain breached around 4 pm in Rajarajeshwari Nagar, sending water gushing into houses after KSNDMC recorded over 100 mm of rain.
After overnight flooding, the Chief Minister said in RR Nagar that stormwater drain works were incomplete and there were about 20 drain bottlenecks in RR Nagar.

name: RR Nagar Arch junction, Mysuru Road

events.summary: The BBMP control room received complaints of waterlogging near the RR Nagar arch during heavy rain.
Sewage mixing with rainwater in the Vrishabhavathi valley flooded Mysuru Road in Nayandahalli, submerging the road to the metro station.
Floodwater rose to dangerous levels and almost submerged buses near Nayandahalli.
BBMP's control room reported waterlogging at Nayandahalli and Kengeri among other areas.
The stormwater drain at Jnanabharathi overflowed onto Mysuru Road, clogging the Nayandahalli junction and blocking the road.

name: Global Village Tech Park (behind RV College)

events.summary: The Global Village Tech Park in Rajarajeshwari Nagar behind RV College of Engineering was submerged in an evening downpour.

name: Mysuru Road at Dubasipalya / RV College

events.summary: The Dubasipalya drain overflowed because the pipe under Mysuru Road was too small, inundating the highway and disrupting traffic for over an hour.
Waterlogging slowed traffic at Kengeri, RV College and Jayaramdas junction on Mysuru Road.
Heavy inflow into the Vrishabhavathi washed away a major portion of its retaining wall near Mylasandra on Mysuru Road, affecting traffic.
BBMP deployed two tractors to move residents in and out of the Kendriya Vihar apartment complex, which was under about three feet of water. The complex is next to Yelahanka lake and floods often.
Kendriya Vihar apartments in Yelahanka flooded for the third time in a month.

After heavy overnight rain Rainbow Drive and the Sarjapur Road and Outer Ring Road area were flooded, with large sections of main roads under water. The layout sits in a valley between Halanayakanahalli and Junnasandra lakes.

name: Outer Ring Road at Ecospace, Bellandur

events.summary: Two to three feet of water on the Outer Ring Road from Silk Board junction to Bellandur, Marathahalli and Sarjapura Road after heavy overnight rain.
Roads leading to the Marathahalli flyover were under water, cutting it off to vehicles, after 131.6 mm of overnight rain (IMD).
Standing water stopped traffic at Silk Board junction; service roads and the adjoining underpasses flooded after about 105 mm of rain in 24 hours.
Flood water entered houses in HSR Layout after torrential overnight rain; boats and tractor-trolleys were used in the worst stretches.
A day after the deluge, ST Bed Layout in Koramangala was still flooded; water had entered homes.

Hosur Road was waterlogged between Chandapura Circle and Bommasandra, with queues on the roads linking Electronics City to Hosur Road; commuters said the Electronic City flyover flooded within 30 minutes of rain.
Traffic advisory for waterlogging at the Hebbal flyover upper ramp towards the city and the down ramp towards the airport after overnight rain.
Heavy Sunday rain flooded the K R Circle underpass; water rose to the windows of a car carrying seven people and a 22-year-old woman drowned, and two auto-rickshaws also got stuck.
After overnight rain on 14-15 August, a resident's photo from Guptha Layout in Ulsoor showed two cars and several motorbikes under water.

A Friday flash flood forced residents of about 70 low-lying houses in Kanakanagar, Fayazabad, Kumaraswamy Layout and Yelachenahalli to evacuate; in Fayazabad water swept away furniture and submerged parked vehicles.
Friday-evening rain left traders in the Chikpet, Sultanpet, Mamulpet and Old Tharagupet market streets wading through knee-deep water.
All-night rain from 1.15 am to 10 am fully flooded the railway underpass near Sivananda Circle in Seshadripuram, making commuting a nightmare; a resident said the intersection keeps flooding.
After all-night rain, a commuter reported knee-deep water near Mekhri Circle at 9.30 am with traffic at a standstill.
Early-Sunday rain (48.2 mm per IMD) left the city railway station and Kempegowda Bus Station looking like a lake from severe waterlogging, disrupting bus and train services.
During heavy Friday-evening rain that inundated about 30 western and northern localities, water gushed into the basement car park of Mantri Square mall in Malleswaram.
Overnight rain overwhelmed several shops on Commercial Street and in Sampangirama Nagar; shopkeepers were pumping out flooded floors and removing soaked goods until Monday afternoon.
A Koramangala 6th Block resident said roads flooded within 30 minutes of rain starting at 11 pm and water entered houses by midnight, forcing families to move out.
Record overnight rain on 18-19 May (105.5 mm at the IMD city station by 8.30 am) inundated the BMTC bus depot at Shantinagar and flooded the ground floor of the CCB office in Shanthinagar.
Friday rain caused waterlogging at 38 locations per traffic police, including the Okalipuram underpass and nearby Binny Mill Junction.
The Epsilon gated villa community was among the upscale complexes worst hit by two days of torrential early-September rain, with residents evacuated on tractors.
After overnight rain on 4-5 September 2022, inflatable boats were deployed to rescue people on the Balagere-Panathur road near the Sekhar Bellevue apartment.
The road opposite Disha apartment in Balagere, Panathur was inundated with thigh-deep rainwater as vehicles tried to cross on the morning of 5 September 2022.
Traffic police reported the Kadubeesanahalli underpass completely filled with rainwater after heavy rain on the night of 12 June 2023.
A breach in the Hulimavu Lake bund on the afternoon of 24 November 2019 sent water into several houses in Hulimavu Layout; NDRF personnel were deployed.
Rain late on 14 August and early on 15 August 2017 (184 mm recorded in Bilekahalli) sent water into many homes in areas including Bilekahalli and Anugraha Layout.

name: Madhuvana Apartment, NS Palya, BTM 2nd Stage

events.summary: During heavy May 2025 rain, two people were electrocuted while pumping rainwater out of the basement of Madhuvana Apartment in NS Palya, BTM Layout 2nd Stage.
Overnight rain on 29-30 August 2022 flooded Sunny Brooks layout on Sarjapur Road after a stormwater drain overflowed, partially submerging trees, shops and houses.
Overnight rain on 29-30 August 2022 inundated multiple houses in Shanthinikethan Colony, Munekolala, with 2-3 feet of water as stormwater-drain encroachments remained.
Overnight rain on 29-30 August 2022 submerged multiple tin-shed houses in the Thubrahalli Palaya area near BEML Layout in about 3 feet of water.
After the overnight downpour of May 18-19, Sai Layout in Horamavu was among the worst-affected areas, with its streets submerged under four to five feet of water.

name: Kuvempu Nagar and Basava Samithi Layout, Doddabommasandra

events.summary: Doddabommasandra lake overflowed after the 21 October cloudburst, and water reached up to four feet inside homes and on roads in Kuvempu Nagar and Basava Samithi Layout.
Tatanagar was among north Bengaluru areas flooded after the October 21 heavy rain, with water at some locations reaching as high as six feet.
Bhadrappa Layout was among north Bengaluru areas flooded after the October 21 heavy rain, with water at some locations reaching as high as six feet.
Ramanashree California was among the layouts and apartments the Deputy Chief Minister listed as inundated after overnight rain in which Yelahanka received 157 mm in six hours.
Manyata Tech Park was under water after Monday's downpour; roads inside the park flooded and employees who could not drive in were sent home.
Manyata Tech Park near Hebbal was waterlogged by about 8.30 pm on Monday evening, stranding people as surrounding roads were inundated.
Tuesday night rain flooded parts of HBR Layout, with water entering residents' houses and the corporator arranging pumps the next morning.
Overflowing stormwater drains caused waterlogging in HBR Layout during the overnight downpour of May 18-19.
After the Dorekere lake breached in overnight rain, over 200 houses in Saptagiri, Lakshmaiah and Lakkanna Layouts behind Subramanyapura police station were flooded in the early hours of Monday.
Houses in MLA Layout at Kalena Agrahara off Bannerghatta Road were flooded in the overnight downpour, which residents blamed on a breached stormwater drain nearby.
JP Nagar 9th Phase at Avalahalli was among the places where homes were inundated after the record overnight rain of 23-24 September 2018.
Water logged some homes in Jayanagar 4th T Block after heavy rainfall, according to a Deccan Herald report on the September 2018 rain.
Waterlogging was reported inside some homes in AGS Layout at Ittamadu after heavy rainfall in September 2018.
Saturday afternoon rain caused waterlogging in front of Banashankari metro station, and rainwater seeping into the station caused chaos there.
Monday evening's heavy showers left RV Road waterlogged in front of Vijaya College near Lalbagh.
Waterlogging on Hosur Main Road near Roopena Agrahara caused traffic snarls in the early hours of Sunday after overnight thundershowers.
An overflowing stormwater drain in Roopena Agrahara left at least four feet of water on the road and badly hit city-bound traffic, police said.
After torrential overnight rain, traffic police closed the Electronics City flyover because of waterlogging at Roopena Agrahara.
Heavy overnight rain from Saturday into Sunday inundated the railway tracks at Kengeri station.
Friday's heavy rain left parts of south-east Bengaluru severely waterlogged, with Neeladri Nagar in Electronic City among the worst-hit areas.
Heavy Thursday-evening rain flooded low-lying areas around Kamakhya theatre in Vidyapeetha ward, the worst-hit spot, where nearly 80 houses were inundated.
In the same downpour, a Wilson Garden residents' association member said roads from 3rd to 8th Cross were inundated and sewage flowed back into houses.
Sunday's thunderstorm overwhelmed the encroached Bellandur canal and its connecting drains, and floodwater burst into homes in Spice Garden Layout.
Monday evening rain left East Bengaluru worst hit, with waterlogging reported on Spice Garden Road along with Marathahalli Bridge and Varthur Main Road.
A weekend downpour before 1 October 2024 flooded parts of East Bengaluru, including The Spice Garden in Marathahalli, which houses over 200 paying guest accommodations.
After Saturday's heavy rain, sewage-blackened water from Bellandur Lake spilled onto the roads of Kariammana Agrahara, which connects to the Outer Ring Road.
Sunday's thunderstorm overwhelmed the encroached Bellandur canal, and massive amounts of water inundated Kariyammana Agrahara along with Yamalur, Marathahalli and Varthur.
In a weekend downpour before 1 October 2024, Muneshwara Temple Road and ECC Road in Whitefield flooded because of stormwater drains residents say developers encroached.
Heavy Monday evening rain sent water into at least four houses on Kalamma Road in Kammanahalli, according to BBMP control room complaints.
In the same Monday evening downpour, rainwater entered more than two houses located behind the Banaswadi railway station.
Monday evening's heavy rain inundated seven houses in Kaveri Nagar in Kaval Byrasandra.
Sunday evening rainfall caused waterlogging and traffic congestion on Domlur Main Road, among several spots across the city.
Traffic police closed the Bhoopasandra underpass on Monday night because it was inundated by heavy overnight rain.
Traffic police closed the Sahakarnagar underpass on Monday night because it was inundated by heavy overnight rain.
A heavy night-time downpour (reported as Wednesday night) waterlogged several low-lying areas, including Nandidurg Road, Kalyan Nagar, Banaswadi and Kasturi Nagar, with blocked drains blamed.
A heavy downpour in the early hours of Tuesday flooded houses in HAL 2nd Stage, Indiranagar, with drain water entering homes and damaging furniture.
After heavy Sunday-night rain in the Yelahanka Zone, KSNDMC data showed severe street inundation at Kogilu Cross, and rainwater entered many homes in the area.
